goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — embed_url` is not synchronously validated, so malformed or off-host requests get a 200 loading page that reloads and re-enqueues forever instead of an actionable 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the embed_controller.rb code, the `best` action calls `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which returns nil for non-existent URLs, then enqueues a job and renders 'loading'. The loading.html.erb page has a 30-second auto-reload. The job (retrieve_topic.rb) calls TopicRetriever which checks `invalid_host?` - if the host doesn't match embeddable_host, it returns early without creating anything. So for off-host URLs, the job does nothing, no TopicEmbed is created, and the page keeps reloading forever. For malformed URLs, URI parsing would fail in TopicRetriever.invalid_host? which catches the exception and returns true (invalid), so again nothing happens. This is a real issue - users with off-host or malformed URLs get stuck in an infinite reload loop rather than receiving an error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — Removing the public `--category`/`-c` option breaks existing Disqus import commands and prevents callers from retaining their requested category.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the `--category` option is indeed removed from line 117 (method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: 'The category to post in') and the corresponding code that uses it (lines 144-147 setting category_id and line 150 passing category: category_id to PostCreator) is also removed. The import method now uses TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator.new, which doesn't accept a category parameter. This is a breaking change for existing users who relied on the --category flag to specify which category their imported Disqus content should go into. The functionality is genuinely removed with no replacement, which would break existing import workflows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Replacing XML-backed topic creation with `import_remote` makes the importer abort on an unavailable source page, so a complete Disqus export is no longer sufficient.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code created a post with `PostCreator.new(user, title: t[:title], raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]", ...)` which embedded the link as raw content. The new code calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` which in topic_embed.rb uses `open(url).read` to fetch the remote page content via HTTP. This means the importer now requires the original source URLs to be accessible at import time, whereas before it only needed the Disqus XML export file. If the source pages are unavailable (site down, pages deleted, etc.), the import will fail. This is a real behavioral change that could break imports for users who have complete Disqus exports but whose source pages are no longer available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Calling `import_remote` drops the thread's exported `created_at`, dating each imported topic's first post at migration time and corrupting chronology.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code at line 144-145 was: `creator = PostCreator.new(user, title: t[:title], raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]", created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` which passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The new code at line 144 is: `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. Looking at the `import_remote` method in app/models/topic_embed.rb, it only accepts `user`, `url`, and `opts` (which can contain `title`). It then calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, opts[:title] || doc.title, doc.content)`. The `import` method creates posts via `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` - there's no `created_at` parameter being passed. So the finding is correct: the thread's `created_at` from the Disqus export (stored in `t[:created_at]`) is no longer being used, and imported topics will have their creation date set to the migration time instead of the original post date.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — The URL absolutizer handles only root-relative paths, leaving ordinary relative links and images pointed at the Discourse embed route.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` for links and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` for images. This means it only handles root-relative paths (starting with '/') and does NOT handle ordinary relative paths like 'images/wat.jpg' or 'hello.html' (without leading slash). The finding is correct - relative URLs that don't start with '/' will not be converted to absolute URLs, leaving them potentially broken or pointing to wrong locations when embedded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — Exact-string URL lookup treats equivalent forms such as trailing-slash or fragment variants as different articles and can create duplicate discussions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in topic_embed.rb, the `topic_id_for_embed` method at line 79 does a simple `where(embed_url: embed_url)` lookup. The `import` method also uses `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` for checking existing embeds. This means URLs like 'http://example.com/page' vs 'http://example.com/page/' vs 'http://example.com/page#section' would be treated as different URLs and could create duplicate topics for the same content. This is a real correctness issue - URL normalization is not performed, so semantically equivalent URLs could result in duplicate discussions being created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Appending attribution in place mutates the caller's content string, so reusing it causes duplicate footers and spurious revisions.

adjudication.rationale:
Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb:13, the line `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` uses `<<` which mutates the original string in place. However, examining the callers: (1) poll_feed.rb passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which creates a new string each time, (2) import_remote passes `doc.content` from Readability which is also a fresh string. The finding claims 'reusing it causes duplicate footers' but there's no evidence in the diff that the same content string is reused across multiple calls. Each call to import() receives a fresh string. While mutating the parameter is not ideal practice, it doesn't cause the specific bug described (duplicate footers and spurious revisions) based on the actual usage patterns shown in the diff.
